submitter: site_delivery_and_editor lane, fixing bugs_open/466 — the approve-to-apply path, met for the first time on the first paid site (boxingonline, 2026-09-03).
rationale:
ROUND 3. Round 2 returned REVISE again, gated by prior_art_librarian, with four real defects between the seats. All four are fixed, and two of them were things I would otherwise have shipped wrong.

THE GATING OBJECTION FOUND THE RIGHT ANSWER RESTING ON THE WRONG EVIDENCE. My blast-radius scan used jsonb_each(default_config->'workflow'->'steps') — a TOP-LEVEL walk, which LANDMINES documents as blind to any step nested inside a sub_workflow. Re-run RECURSIVELY: still exactly ONE consumer (copy-editor / workflow.steps.request_review), zero others, sub-workflows included. The claim held. The evidence for it did not, and the seat was right to refuse the weaker version — I had read that very landmine earlier in the same session and still wrote the blind idiom.

THE ONE I WOULD HAVE SHIPPED WRONG (editquality): my new moved-target REFUSAL rested on page_components.updated_at, and LANDMINES states plainly that this column CANNOT make the claim 'the copy changed' — at least two live writers bump it with no copy touched at all, one of them PAGE-WIDE (a single review write moves updated_at on every component of the page). Refusing on it would decline perfectly fresh approvals, and my '0 of 31 stale today' measurement cannot rule that out going forward, because it describes today's state and not what a future status write will do. The arm is DOWNGRADED from refuse to WARN: the item is filed, and the approver gets both the doubt and an explicit statement that it is not proof. The columns that COULD answer it — content_hash, rendered_html_digest, which move only when content does — need a BASELINE that no proposal records. Recording one is the PROPOSER's change (copy-editor), not this handler's, and that is now said out loud in the code rather than quietly wished for. Deletion stays a hard refusal, because that claim the data can make.

THE TEST THAT WAS TOO WEAK TO HOLD ITS OWN FIX (editquality). Round 1's gating fix required follow_on_item_ids to be a present-and-empty []. A nil []string marshals to `null`, and `null` decodes to a zero-length assertion exactly as `[]` does — so round 2's test could not tell them apart. The slice was already initialised correctly; the TEST was the defect. doApprove now returns the raw body and asserts the literal "follow_on_item_ids":[]. Mutating the declaration back to `var followOnIDs []string` now kills it, which it did not before. The seat reasoned this out from a sketch.

PARTIAL BATCHES (bug_historian): a per-element INSERT failure vanished into a Warn, leaving follow_on_item_ids quietly one short — a partial completion reporting success, which is the shape this whole change exists to remove. It now lands in skipped_edits with its error, so an admin does not have to COUNT to notice.

BATCH GROUPING (prior_art_librarian): site_work_items.batch_id already IS the platform's convention for N items minted from one source event — [MEASURED 2026-09-03] 25,880 of 29,851 rows carry one across 4,161 batches. One approval's children now share one. The seat was right that I had answered 'is there prior art for fanning out' without asking 'is there prior art for GROUPING the results'.

PROVENANCE (tooling_provenance): the RFC_022 escalation trigger — a SECOND live consumer of fan_out_from comes back as needs_rfc, not another same-commit wiring — is filed as an addendum to RFC_022 itself, with the recursive census query, so it is not re-derived from a council submission's prose. Committed a1b2b4283.

Nine mutations across three rounds, all killed. Unchanged and still the argument for shipping: [MEASURED 2026-09-03] 42 include_fields mentions across 21 items since 2026-08-24, ZERO ever resolvable; 16 review items parked carrying 31 edits nobody can currently approve.

plan.summary: Repair `include_fields` (fall back to the approved body when the review spec cannot hold the name — which, measured, is always), and add two opt-in keys to `on_approve`: `fan_out_from` (file one follow-on per element of a named array in the approved data, merging that element's fields at the top of the child spec) and `defaults` (fields the proposal does not carry). Refuse and REPORT a fanned-out element whose page_component_id no longer exists, rather than filing an item guaranteed to die. Record what the approval actually produced on the review row, so `complete` stops being the only thing the approver sees.

edits.rationale: include_fields consults `spec` FIRST (documented semantics preserved exactly — nothing that resolves today can change) and the admin's submitted body second. A name absent from both is now ABSENT from the child spec rather than written as an explicit null; the observed damage was `copy_edit: null, page_target: null`, a shape that reads as real, empty content.

One follow-on per element. Merge order is defaults, then include_fields, then the element's own fields, then the provenance fields LAST — so an element carrying its own `approved_by` or `source_item_id` cannot overwrite who approved it. Children do not duplicate the whole approved payload; `source_item_id` points at the review row, which holds it. ROUND 2: createFollowOn is the SINGLE creation path — the fan-out calls the same closure the single-item branch calls, N times, not a second inserter (reuse_agent). [MEASURED 2026-09-03] idx_swi_dedup excludes NULL item_key, which this handler has never set, so N children cannot collide; a per-element key is deliberately NOT minted because it would turn a cannot-happen into a can-fail-at-insert (guidelines). An EMPTY or wrong-typed array is the gating case and is now pinned by a test: nothing filed, and fan_out_note says why.

ROUND 3, acting on editquality: the address rots two ways but only ONE is a claim the data can make. DELETED is answerable and is REFUSED (no row for that id on this site). MOVED is NOT: page_components.updated_at is bumped by status-only writers, one of them page-wide, so it means 'might have moved', never 'did move' (LANDMINES). That arm now WARNS and still files, handing the approver the doubt plus an explicit note that it is not proof — rather than manufacturing a false refusal. A real refusal needs a digest baseline recorded at proposal time, which is copy-editor's change, not this handler's. TOCTOU on the existence check is stated, not engineered around.

466 candidate 3. A review row reading `complete` while its spawned work failed is 'a complete work item is not a repaired artefact' aimed at a PERSON. The row's result now carries follow_on_items[], skipped_edits[] and fan_out_note; `follow_on_item` is kept for existing readers and names the first. follow_on_item_ids is ALWAYS present in the response, so 'nothing was filed' is a visible [] rather than an absent key that reads as success.

Eight tests. NINE mutations across three rounds, all killed — not one test was accepted on green alone: remove the dead-address guard · remove the approved-body fallback · make fan-out unconditional · drop the element-field merge · neuter the moved-target arm · drop the empty-array note · declare followOnIDs as a nil slice · drop the insert-failure record · never raise a stale warning. The nil-slice mutation is the one worth noting: it SURVIVED round 2's version of the test and dies against round 3's, which is the difference between asserting a length and asserting the wire format.

The config half. Replaces the two names that can never resolve with `domain` (a key the review spec genuinely holds, and what the two proven hand-filed items carried), adds fan_out_from='edits' and defaults={edit_type:'content_edit'}. [MEASURED 2026-09-03] of the 41 proposed edits across those 21 items, 41 carry page_component_id, ZERO carry edit_type, ZERO carry page_name — so edit_type must be defaulted and page_name must NOT be, because every edit is addressed by page_component_id and a defaulted page_name would be a guess applied to every page. Snapshot table, anchor guard that aborts if the step has drifted or fan_out_from is already present, and a DO/RAISE verify (a verify block of bare SELECTs cannot stop the COMMIT). ROUND 2 (guardian): filed as config_change, not add — the SQL file is the vehicle, but the SURFACE being changed is copy-editor's request_review step config in agent_definitions.default_config. The anchor guard's exact predicate: it aborts unless exactly one live copy-editor row exists, on_approve is present at workflow.steps.request_review.config, its item_type is section_edit and handler_agent is section-editor, and fan_out_from is NOT already present.

grounded_in: checkpoint_for_review_action.go:157-180 — the review item spec is a FIXED key set: review_data, checkpoint, source_agent, correlation_id, then optionally domain, spec_aspect, on_approve. No arbitrary field can reach it.

(The `complete` bucket's 4-of-4 'stale' reading is artefactual — applying an edit is what bumps updated_at — so that arm of the test discriminates only for unapplied items.)

The other on_approve producer is fork_theme_from_site_action.go:329-337, whose on_approve is {update_theme, update_collection}: no item_type, no include_fields, no `checkpoint: true` — so HandleApproveWorkItem 400s it and it never reaches this code. It is unaffected, and it is the whole of the rest of the population.
